messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall - High error rate and 95th latency spike for customer Nightingale Health (VPC-115d) on dedicated pool 'dl-pool-7'. Error: 503 upstream_timeout. Alerting rule: infra.dedicated.pool.errors > 5% (5m).

oncall-ash: on it. taking pager. joining bridge. allocating 15m initial. can someone drop recent deploys?

sre-jamie: no deploys in last 20m to that pool according to deploy-bot. seeing CPU and nvme IO spikes on nodes in pool dl-pool-7. possible noisy-tenant. pulling tenant map.

eng-runtime-carlos: confirming tail of logs for Nightingale's router: `upstream timeout after 30s` followed by `kvcache miss backlog`. looks like cache thrash + a small subset of requests are causing long decoding times.

incident-bot: (system) Bridge created: https://meet.redwood/incident/1930456789. Runbook: dedicated-pool-isolation v2.

oncall-ash: @sre-jamie run tenant isolation on dl-pool-7 for Nightingale and any high-QPS tenants. we prefer soft isolation first (rate-limit + circuit) to avoid full eviction.

sre-jamie: running soft isolation - applying policy now. command: ```rcli pools apply-policy dl-pool-7 --tenant nightingale --policy "soft-isolate:rate=0.2,concurrency=2"```

eng-runtime-carlos: applying temporary model fallback for Nightingale's route to smaller quantized variant (gptq-8b) to reduce decode cost. updating routing: ```routes update nightingale/route0 --model gptq-8b --ttl 10m```

acct-manager-priya: I pinged Nightingale PO via DM, they're aware and on standby for joint comms. tonight@nightingale is on the bridge.

customer-rep-nightingale: we see a spike on our side too, some jobs retrying. appreciate update. are you doing anything that might drop requests?

oncall-ash: no request drops expected with soft isolate. we'll throttle heavy callers first then fall back to model variant. aim is no 100% failures. will post timeline.

eng-runtime-carlos: KV cache hit rate for Nightingale dropped from 82% -> 21% over last 4m. suspect a batch of long-context logs triggered cache churn. starting prefix cache warming for recent prefixes.```

sre-jamie: nodes with nvme iowait high: node-12 and node-15. set cordon and migrate non-nightingale tenants off node-12,15. command: ```k8s cordon node-12 && k8s drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data```

oncall-ash: status?

eng-runtime-carlos: cordon+drain kicked. migrations started. CPU on nodes trending down. latency 95th dropping from 2.5s -> 700ms. error rate reduced to 1.1%.

incident-bot: (system) Page severity lowered to P2 at 1930458450 based on back-to-normal policy.

cs-zoe: starting customer-impact assessment for Nightingale: which orgs affected (prod/dev), % requests failed, and any SLA thresholds breached. Priya, want me to draft a customer note?

acct-manager-priya: yes pls. include ETA for RCA and whether credits are expected. Nightingale is on enterprise contract with 99.95% SLA for uptime and 99% for latency p95.

eng-runtime-carlos: quick numbers: production route success dropped to 94.6% for a 12-minute window (192493 -> 203819 requests). p95 latency hit 2.5s for ~9 minutes. will attach metric graphs to RCA.

oncall-ash: quick mitigation summary for timeline: 1930456789 - alert fired; 1930456820 - oncall picked up; 1930456845 - soft isolate policy applied; 1930456900 - model fallback applied; 1930456970 - cordon/drain nodes started; 1930457300 - normalizing; 1930458450 - severity downgraded.

incident-bot: (system) Handoff reminder: if moving to long-running post-incident, create a follow-up ticket in ISSUES-ops with #incident-1930456789.

sre-jamie: creating follow-up: ISSUES-ops-12871 (mitigation and long-term fix). assign eng-runtime-carlos for cache policy improvements and autoscaler tweak.

eng-runtime-carlos: will own cache policy change + routing fallback improvements. initial action items: 1) prefix-based prewarm for Nightingale, 2) reduce KV eviction aggressiveness during peak, 3) add tenant-level QoS for NVMe IO.

cs-zoe: drafting customer message now. proposed text snippet: "We observed intermittent elevated latency and timeouts affecting requests routed to your dedicated pool between HH:MM and HH:MM UTC. Our team applied throttles and temporary model fallback to stabilize traffic while migrating load off unhealthy nodes. We are investigating root cause and will follow up with a detailed RCA and any credits if SLA thresholds were exceeded." Thoughts?

acct-manager-priya: good. add apology + option for a follow-up call with our SRE and product lead. include timeline and next steps.

customer-rep-nightingale: message looks fine. they'd like a brief exec note for their CTO. can we provide a one-paragraph exec summary?

cto-maya: draft exec line: "Redwood experienced transient resource contention in the dedicated pool serving Nightingale that caused elevated latency and some timeout errors. We applied rate limiting and a model fallback to restore normal service while migrating traffic off impacted nodes. We will share a technical RCA and remediation plan within 48 hours, and will propose a customer credit if our SLA thresholds are confirmed breached."

legal-ops: flag: avoid definitive SLA credit promises in exec line. use conditional language: "if SLA thresholds are confirmed breached." good to CC billing.

cs-zoe: noted. preparing 2 versions: exec and engineering. sending DM to @customer-rep-nightingale with both.

sre-jamie: root cause hypothesis for RCA draft: high-cardinality long-context requests caused KV cache churn leading to degraded cache hit rate and NVMe pressure on a subset of nodes. contributing factor: autoscaler didn't trigger early enough due to binned metrics. short-term mitigations applied: soft isolate, model fallback, node cordon/drain, cache prewarm. long-term mitigations proposed: tenant-level IO QoS, cache eviction policy tweak, autoscaler sensitivity tuning, and an alert for cache-hit-rate anomalies.

eng-runtime-carlos: adding one more: consider per-tenant KV cache quotas and a small-percentage of cold-start prewarm on detected prefix spikes.

oncall-ash: recording owners on follow-up ticket: carlos (runtime), jamie (sre), zoe (cs), priya (acct). target RCA draft in 36h.

account-manager-priya: we'll likely offer a one-off credit equivalent to downtime % against monthly committed spend pending RCA math. will coordinate with billing after final numbers.

customer-rep-nightingale: appreciate the transparency. they'd like the RCA and a proposed credit by EOD +48. is that realistic?

eng-runtime-carlos: 36h for draft ok. will include metrics export, logs, and mitigation timeline.

cs-zoe: sending the interim update to Nightingale now (internal copy posted in thread).

cs-zoe: (paste) "Interim update: We detected elevated latency/timeouts affecting requests to your dedicated pool from 2026-03-15T01:26:29Z. Our engineers implemented throttling and a temporary model fallback, and migrated workloads off impacted nodes. Service was stable by ~01:54Z. We're working on an RCA and will follow up with details and any SLA credit calculations within 48 hours. If you'd like a live call, please pick a time and we'll join."

customer-rep-nightingale: forwarded to internal CTO. they'll expect the RCA. thanks.

incident-bot: (system) Incident moved to 'post-incident' state; please update ISSUES-ops-12871 with RCA attachments.

oncall-ash: closing on-call action: put mitigation notes in the ticket, mark handoff to SRE/eng. good job team.

sre-jamie: quick retrospec note: autoscaler metrics are currently aggregated at pool-level; for dedicated pools we should consider tenant-level signals. adding that as priority in ISSUES-ops-12871.

eng-runtime-carlos: will draft RCA outline in the ticket now. cc: @cto-maya for exec review before we send to customer.

acct-manager-priya: once RCA approved, I will coordinate a short credit proposal and a follow-up exec call. leaving thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:

cs-zoe: thanks all. I'll update customer thread and create calendar invite if they want a call.

customer-rep-nightingale: thanks for the quick response. appreciate the follow-through.

oncall-ash: logging final note: incident severity P3, duration ~28m (partial impact window). moving to post-incident runbook.

(End of thread)
